chunks: From him, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaym, from Sulaymān ibn Jaʿfar, from his father, who said:

A man from the people of al-Shām entered upon Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and said to him, “Indeed, the first one to precede to Paradise is Bilāl.” He said, “And why?” He said, “Because he was the first one to give the adhān.”

key_terms.أَذَّنَ: gave the adhān, the call to salat (prayer)
key_terms.أَهْلِ الشَّامِ: the people of al-Shām, indicating the man’s regional origin
key_terms.أَوَّلُ: the first, indicating precedence in rank or action
key_terms.الْجَنَّةِ: Paradise, the abode of divine reward
key_terms.بِلاَلٌ: Bilāl, the early mu’adhdhin of Islam

ai.seo_question: Why is Bilāl said to be the first to precede to Paradise?
ai.summary: This hadith relates that a man from al-Shām told Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام that Bilāl would be the first to precede to Paradise because he was the first to call the adhān. It highlights the virtue and rank associated with initiating and establishing the call to salat (prayer).
